lines: {target}? Black stone and lava leave little mercy.
If anyone heads for Basalt Deltas, this is my advice. Step like every block wants an argument.
Ash and basalt make the Nether feel broken twice.
Basalt Deltas is no small story.
I will remember Basalt Deltas as jagged black country with heat in its cracks.
I would mark down my route before going anywhere near Basalt Deltas.
Before Basalt Deltas, I would count my food and test every torch.
Stillness can hide trouble, so I would stay alert inside Basalt Deltas.
Bring home the story and leave the scratches at Basalt Deltas.
<shake>Pride</shake> makes a poor repair kit when things go wrong at Basalt Deltas.
Tell me we are going to Basalt Deltas and I will start with a strong pick and fireproof blocks.
With lava and broken ground nearby, a loose tool head becomes more than a nuisance.
I would keep some strength in reserve in case of a hostile shape in the smoke, even if the way ahead seemed quiet.
Falling ash is no place to balance a loose rivet on one knee.
I would shorten every loose strap before stepping onto the jagged basalt underfoot.
For Basalt Deltas, I care more about a sound haft than a polished cutting edge.
Tell me what gave out at Basalt Deltas and what would have served you better.
I can prepare a better set for Basalt Deltas now that I know what went wrong.
For another trip to Basalt Deltas, one bent pick can be fixed. A whole pack lost to carelessness cannot.
Every rough trip teaches the smithing table something. Basalt Deltas should teach plenty.
{target}? Red Nether trees grow among hoglins and worse.
If anyone heads for Crimson Forest, this is my advice. Keep gold on and eyes open.
The whole forest looks like it has a pulse.
Crimson Forest is no small story.
I will remember Crimson Forest as a red forest that feels too alive.
Someone should know my return path before I head toward Crimson Forest.
A clear head is worth more than one extra tool around Crimson Forest.
I would pay closest attention when nothing seemed wrong in Crimson Forest.
Coming back safely would be enough reward for visiting Crimson Forest.
<shake>Pride</shake> makes a poor repair kit when things go wrong at Crimson Forest.
Once you mention hoglins charging between crimson stems, my first thought is to leave room to dodge around the fungi.
I would make room for a sharp axe and blocks for cover before setting out for Crimson Forest.
If I had to face lava and broken ground, I'd want every tool tested first.
I would keep the best-fitted tool within reach if a hostile shape in the smoke cut off our return.
I would test my footing on the crimson nylium underfoot before swinging anything heavy.
Would you carry the same tools to Crimson Forest after what happened there?
For another trip to Crimson Forest, good equipment should make hard work possible, not make foolish work safe.
I want a close look at the cutting edge that worked around Crimson Forest.
At Crimson Forest, a sharp edge helps, but a firm handle matters all day.
I would rather carry a spare handle than limp home from Crimson Forest with a useless tool.
{target}? The Nether wastes neither heat nor cruelty.
If anyone heads for Nether Wastes, this is my advice. Watch ghasts, cliffs, and every pool of lava.
Netherrack crumbles like it enjoys the fall.
Nether Wastes is no small story.
I will remember Nether Wastes as red stone and fire with no decent sky.
A journey to Nether Wastes starts with leaving clear directions at home.
A sensible load for Nether Wastes starts with food and dependable torches.
Silence would be another reason to move carefully through Nether Wastes.
The village needs returning travelers more than trophies from Nether Wastes.
<shake>Pride</shake> makes a poor repair kit when things go wrong at Nether Wastes.
Hearing about netherrack giving way quickly beside sudden lava pockets makes me want to tap ahead before opening a tunnel.
For Nether Wastes, I would not object to packing a fast pick and fire-resistant blocks.
A proper bench will do more for damaged gear than fighting with it through falling ash.
The marked route back to the portal matters more than the perfect repair when trouble is moving closer.
The loose netherrack underfoot would tell me which tool stays packed and which one stays ready.
Surviving Nether Wastes does not make a tool sound. Let me inspect it before the next trip.
Let me see the scratches from Nether Wastes. Wear tells its own version of a journey.
You have convinced me to rethink the tool roll for Nether Wastes.
Before heading to Nether Wastes, I'd oil the iron and test every wedge twice.
I cannot tell whether Nether Wastes was harder on your edges or your tool shafts.
{target}? The ground pulls back when you try to leave.
If anyone heads for Soul Sand Valley, this is my advice. Wear good boots and keep ghasts in mind.
Soul sand makes every step feel watched.
Soul Sand Valley is no small story.
I will remember Soul Sand Valley as a valley where the floor does not want guests.
No trip to Soul Sand Valley begins until somebody knows the way back.
The useful supplies go in first when I pack for Soul Sand Valley.
I would trust a careful warning more than easy silence at Soul Sand Valley.
A story from Soul Sand Valley is better when nobody has to hide the injuries.
<shake>Pride</shake> makes a poor repair kit when things go wrong at Soul Sand Valley.
Knowing about soul sand slowing every step under skeleton fire, I'd build the retreat before crossing the open valley.
Lava and broken ground are the sort of trouble that punishes a rushed repair.
A hostile shape in the smoke would be a poor time to discover the axe head was loose.
A repair can wait until the route back to the portal is clear.
The slow soul sand underfoot sounds like a place for a light pack and tools tied down tight.
Someone should check the grips after that trip. Sweat, water, and fear all loosen things around Soul Sand Valley.
I want to inspect the one piece of gear that never failed you at Soul Sand Valley.
Damage on the gear can finish a story about Soul Sand Valley better than guessing can.
After that story about Soul Sand Valley, I would bring wedges, cord, and enough iron for one ugly repair.
Anything that survived Soul Sand Valley should be inspected before it travels again.
{target}? Blue Nether trees make sense feel optional.
If anyone heads for Warped Forest, this is my advice. Keep gold on and eyes off trouble.
Warped wood looks wrong even before it moves.
Warped Forest is no small story.
I will remember Warped Forest as a blue forest that forgot what forests are for.
I would leave my route with someone before setting out for Warped Forest.
I would pack for Warped Forest with enough food, light, and patience.
Quiet would not persuade me that everything was safe at Warped Forest.
I would count a safe return as the finest prize from Warped Forest.
<shake>Pride</shake> makes a poor repair kit when things go wrong at Warped Forest.
Once you mention twisting vines and endermen filling blue-green woods, my first thought is to avoid meeting eyes while clearing a route.
I would make room for an axe and a carved pumpkin kept packed before setting out for Warped Forest.
I'd keep one dependable tool free in case a hostile shape in the smoke blocked the way out.
I would oil and wrap the iron before trusting it to falling ash.
I would keep spare blocks ready along the route back to the portal. Paths fail too.
Has that journey changed the kit you would take back to Warped Forest?
For another trip to Warped Forest, the best field repair is the one you prepared before leaving the bench.
Did the pick, axe, or shovel suffer most on the trip to Warped Forest?
Show me the cutting edge that came back from Warped Forest.
After Warped Forest, what tool do you regret leaving at home?
